concepts.title: Krittika: The Star of Fire
concepts.excerpt: Look up at the Pleiades on a winter night — that small dipper-shape of seven blurred stars in the shoulder of Taurus.

concepts.title: Rohini: The Star of Ascent
concepts.excerpt: A man has twenty-seven wives. He sleeps with each one on a different night of the month, cycling through them as the lunar phases cycle through the sky.

concepts.title: Mrigashira: The Searching Star
concepts.excerpt: A god, furious at his son-in-law's exclusion from a great sacrifice, set fire to the universe with his rage.

concepts.title: Ardra: The Star of Sorrow
concepts.excerpt: A god is born. Before he opens his eyes, before he sees the sky or the gods who will be his siblings, he is crying.

concepts.title: Punarvasu: The Star of Renewal
concepts.excerpt: Think about an archer with an unusual quiver — every arrow she shoots returns to her after it finds its mark.

concepts.title: Pushya: The Star of Nourishment
concepts.excerpt: Look at a cow at milking time. The udder is heavy with the day's nourishment, ready to give freely to the calf, to the farmer, to the village.

concepts.title: Ashlesha: The Clinging Star
concepts.excerpt: Picture a snake coiled at the bottom of a temple staircase, perfectly still.

concepts.title: Magha: The Star of Power
concepts.excerpt: Imagine an empty palace throne room at midnight. The throne itself is lit by one lamp; the rest is in shadow.

concepts.title: Purva Phalguni: The Fruit of the Tree
concepts.excerpt: It is two in the afternoon. The work of the morning is done. There is a hammock strung between two fig trees in the garden, swaying slightly in the warm breeze, and you have been told you may use it.

concepts.title: Uttara Phalguni: The Star of Patronage
concepts.excerpt: You are at a banquet, and you are about to be presented to the king. You are nervous.

concepts.title: Hasta: The Hand
concepts.excerpt: Hold your hand out, palm up. Whatever you have been asking for — put it there.

concepts.title: Chitra: The Star of Opportunity
concepts.excerpt: Imagine a workshop at the centre of the universe. A craftsman sits at a long table piled with materials — gold, gems, lightning-fragments, the bones of cosmic animals, the pigments of sunsets.

concepts.title: Swati: The Self-Going Star
concepts.excerpt: Walk into a meadow. There is a single blade of grass standing taller than the others, bent slightly in the breeze.

concepts.title: Vishakha: The Star of Purpose
concepts.excerpt: Picture an archway covered in green leaves, the kind a wedding procession passes through.

concepts.title: Anuradha: The Star of Success
concepts.excerpt: You are looking at the surface of a pond. The water is muddy — yellow-brown, clogged with leaves and silt.

concepts.title: Jyeshtha: The Chief or Elder Star
concepts.excerpt: There is a story Pai tells about Moon, the husband of 27 wives (the 27 nakshatras).

concepts.title: Mula: The Foundation Star
concepts.excerpt: Pull a plant out of the ground. Look at what was hidden under the surface — the tangled bunch of roots that anchored the visible plant.

concepts.title: Purva Ashadha: The Invincible Star
concepts.excerpt: Imagine an archer drawing a bow at the edge of an ocean. The bow is curved like a half-moon.

concepts.title: Uttara Ashadha: The Universal Star
concepts.excerpt: Imagine a moment in the celestial calendar when the sun reaches its annual peak — the day the Indian festival Makara Sankranti celebrates, when the Sun transitions to Capricorn and spring begins on the subcontinent.

concepts.title: Shravana: The Star of the Learning Ear
concepts.excerpt: Sit in a quiet room and close your eyes. Listen — not for words, not for outside sounds, but for the underneath sound.

concepts.title: Dhanishtha: The Star of Symphony
concepts.excerpt: Hear a drumbeat from across a field at dusk. The first time you cannot quite tell where it is coming from; the second time you realise it has been holding the rhythm of everything around you without your noticing.

concepts.title: Shatabhisha: The Hundred Stars
concepts.excerpt: A patient is too sick for one doctor. The first doctor tries everything and fails.

concepts.title: Purva Bhadrapada: The Burning Pair
concepts.excerpt: A funeral cot is the bed on which the dead are carried. Two front legs of a funeral cot are what you see when you stand at the head of the procession — the two pillars that hold up the journey-of-the-dead.

concepts.title: Uttara Bhadrapada: The Warrior Star
concepts.excerpt: A serpent lies at the bottom of the deepest ocean, coiled so still you would miss it on first inspection.

concepts.title: Revati: The Wealthy Star
concepts.excerpt: A lighthouse stands at the edge of the world, and a ferryman stands at the foot of a river that separates the living from the dead.

concepts.title: Punch Brahma Mantras: The Five Faces of Śiva's Revelation
concepts.excerpt: Five Vedic mantras assigned to Śiva's five faces, each representing a different dimension of cosmic revelation.

concepts.title: The Inner Guru — Shiva as Your True Teacher
concepts.excerpt: The teaching distinguishes between two gurus: the guru who appears as a human being (the outer guru) and the guru who is consciousness itself (the inner guru).

concepts.title: Rudra-Shiva: The Howler Becoming Auspicious
concepts.excerpt: The deity who would become Shiva — "the Auspicious One" — was born from Brahmā's frustrated frown.

concepts.title: Shiva and Shakti — Non-Dual Polarity
concepts.excerpt: Imagine a mirror. By itself, it's inert — a reflective surface that does nothing.

concepts.title: Shiva Siddhānta — South Indian Dualist Śaivism
concepts.excerpt: Shiva Siddhānta (śaiva siddhānta = the established doctrine / proven conclusion of the Śaivas) is the dominant Śaiva tradition of South India, particularly Tamil Nadu.

concepts.title: Gopeshvara Mahadeva: Shiva as Gopī (Gaudiya Devotional)
concepts.excerpt: In the middle of a full-moon-lit autumn night, Śrī Kṛṣṇa held the magnificent dance of rāsa — manifesting infinite romantic beauty in Vṛndāvana.

concepts.title: Kāmadeva: God of Lust Burned by Shiva's Third Eye
concepts.excerpt: Most Vedic deities have bodies. They walk, drink soma, fight wars, marry consorts, ride carriers across the cosmic-skies.

concepts.title: Raseśvara Shaivism — Mercury Alchemy as Shaiva Path
concepts.excerpt: Selvalingam introduces Raseśvara Shaivism with the energy of someone naming a school most of his audience has never heard of:

concepts.title: Garuḍa: Eagle King, Vahana of Vishnu, Soma-Stealer, Naga-Enemy
concepts.excerpt: Garuḍa is the gigantic king of eagles. He is Vishnu's vāhana — the carrier-mount on which Vishnu travels through the cosmos.

concepts.title: Nārāyaṇa Kavaca: Mystical Armor of Vishnu Names
concepts.excerpt: The Nārāyaṇa Kavaca is "a mystical coat of armor composed of mantra (incantations) dedicated to Vishnu."

concepts.title: Śeṣa-Ananta: Cosmological Serpent, Vishnu's Bed, and Balarāma
concepts.excerpt: Imagine the cosmic ocean before any creation has taken form. Vishnu reclines on its surface.

concepts.title: Govardhana Mountain-Lifting: Krishna as Six-Year-Old Umbrella
concepts.excerpt: Krishna is six or seven years old.

concepts.title: Two Rādhās: Vishakha-Anuradha and the Atharva Veda 19.7 Gaudiya Historical Rooting
concepts.excerpt: DiCara presents one of his most theologically-consequential etymological-claims at the Vishakha chapter and develops it in the Anuradha chapter.

concepts.title: Vishnu as Pervading Sattva and 22 Incarnations
concepts.excerpt: The Sanskrit word viṣṇu literally means "that which is everywhere." Not "the God who is everywhere" — the word itself names a property, all-pervasiveness, that then attaches to the deity.

concepts.title: Mystical-Armor-Lineage: Dadhīci → Aśvinī → Maya → Vishvarupa → Indra Transmission
concepts.excerpt: Follow the Nārāyaṇa Kavaca through DiCara's book and the lineage of who-taught-whom walks across four separate nakshatras.

concepts.title: Sūrya: The Sun God and the Clone-Wife Saṃjña Narrative
concepts.excerpt: Sūrya is the Sun god. The actual-physical-Sun-as-deity. This is structurally distinct from Savitā (the god of sunrise + the abstract-principle-of-cognition-bestowing, deity of Hasta).

concepts.title: Savitā: God of Sunrise, Awakener, and Brahma Gayatri Origin
concepts.excerpt: The Sanskrit word savitā means the awakener. It's built from the root su — "to inspire."

concepts.title: Aditi as Universal Mother of Eight Ādityas
concepts.excerpt: The Sanskrit word aditi literally means boundless — without divisions, undivided, whole.

concepts.title: Mitra: Daytime-Sky God and Love-as-Law
concepts.excerpt: The Sanskrit word mitra has two possible derivations, and DiCara presents both because they reinforce each other:

concepts.title: Aryamā: Foremost Pitr and Divine Matchmaker
concepts.excerpt: The word aryamā literally means dear friend — but the exact, most specific meaning is much narrower.

concepts.title: Bhaga and the Six Traits of Bhagavān: Parāśara's Definition
concepts.excerpt: The Sanskrit word bhaga carries five overlapping meanings: a patron (gracious, generous lord); good fortune, prosperity, happiness; beauty and loveliness; love, lust, Eros; vulva.

concepts.title: Pūṣan: God of Protection, Vegetarian Deity, and the Pūṣan-Vishnu Conjecture
concepts.excerpt: The Sanskrit word pūṣan means "one who nourishes, bringing growth and abundance."

concepts.title: Vishvedeva: Ten or Twelve Deities, Children of Viśvā
concepts.excerpt: Viśva literally means "all, every." Deva means "divinity."

concepts.title: Yama as God of Restriction, Not Just Death
concepts.excerpt: The standard English-language framing of Yama: "the god of death." That's not quite right.

concepts.title: Varuṇa: Night-Sky God and Watcher of Hidden Affairs
concepts.excerpt: The name Varuṇa literally means The All-Enveloping Sky. His home star is Śatabhiṣaj — "Hundreds of Healers" — whose symbol is an empty or dark circle.

concepts.title: Nirṛti: Goddess of Destruction and Wife of Adharma
concepts.excerpt: The Sanskrit word nirṛti has two parts: nir- ("without") + ṛta ("true, luminous, proper, right, lawful").

concepts.title: Bagalamukhi Devī — The Goddess Who Seizes the Tongue
concepts.excerpt: Imagine a war in which your opponent's most dangerous weapon is not a sword or cannon but a word.

concepts.title: Dakṣa Prajāpati: Father of 13 Cosmic Wives and the Yajña Destruction
concepts.excerpt: Dakṣa is one of Brahmā's sons. He is called Prajāpati — "progenitor" — an honorific shared with Brahmā and Kaśyapa.

concepts.title: 33 Vedic Deities: The Trayastrimsa Pantheon
concepts.excerpt: The Vedic apparatus is sometimes summarised as 33 deities ruling everything.

concepts.title: Anugraha and Nigraha — Divine Grace and Concealment
concepts.excerpt: God plays both sides. She reveals you to yourself through grace. She conceals you from yourself through delusion.

concepts.title: Tale of Creation: Primordial Egg, Vishnu, Brahmā Cosmology
concepts.excerpt: DiCara reaches the Rohini chapter — the star of Brahmā the creator — and pauses to deliver the most-developed cosmology in the entire book.

concepts.title: Agni as Ritual Fire and Cross-Chapter Transformation Deity
concepts.excerpt: Agni is the god of fire. Fire has two qualities: it is bright, and it is hot.

concepts.title: Brihaspati: Priest of the Gods and Guru of Prayer
concepts.excerpt: Brihaspati is the god of prayer. He is the priest and guru of all the gods.

concepts.title: Dadhīci: Sage Master of the Nārāyaṇa Kavaca Whose Bones Became the Thunderbolt
concepts.excerpt: Most Vedic sages teach knowledge. Dadhīci does too. But Dadhīci is the only sage in the entire Vedic-mythological corpus whose body itself becomes a cosmic-weapon through self-sacrifice.

concepts.title: Kaśyapa: The Genetic Engineer of the Universe
concepts.excerpt: DiCara introduces Kaśyapa at the Aśleṣā chapter with a striking epithet: "Kaśyapa, the 'genetic engineer of the universe.'

concepts.title: Indra as King of Gods: Rising and Falling Across Textual Strata
concepts.excerpt: Indra is the king of paradise.

concepts.title: Karttikeya: Six-Mothered God of War, Birth from Krittika Mythology
concepts.excerpt: The birth-narrative of Karttikeya is one of the most-complex parentage-cascades in the entire Vedic-mythological corpus.

concepts.title: Tvashta / Vishvakarma / Maya: The Twin Architect Dyad
concepts.excerpt: Some Vedic deities exist in a primordial-abstract form before later taking a concrete shape.

concepts.title: The Eight Vasu: Primordial Elements and the Bhīṣma Curse
concepts.excerpt: The Sanskrit word vasu means "ray of light" and "something of excellence and goodness."

concepts.title: Soma as Fountain of Youth and Elixir of Immortality
concepts.excerpt: Soma is the god of the legendary elixir — also named Soma — that grants eternal youth and unsurpassed delight.

concepts.title: Vāyu as Prāṇa, Oxygen, and the First-Breath Individuating Principle
concepts.excerpt: The standard English-language framing of Vāyu: "god of wind." DiCara: that's incomplete.

concepts.title: Vṛtra: The Anti-God and the Thunderbolt from Dadhīci's Bones
concepts.excerpt: Vṛtra is the monstrous anti-god at the center of the most-developed cross-chapter narrative-arc in DiCara's book.

concepts.title: Central Deity Bindu Principle — Water the Roots, the Whole Yantra Pulses
concepts.excerpt: Your altar has seven mūrtis on it. Gaṇeśa at the entrance. Sūrya behind him.

concepts.title: Deity Visualization Variants: Adapting Inner Form Practice to Your Consciousness
concepts.excerpt: But then practitioners encounter a problem: the visualization doesn't work the same for everyone.

concepts.title: Deity Yoga as Consciousness-Identity Transformation: Becoming the Buddha
concepts.excerpt: In tantric Buddhism, particularly in Tibetan Buddhism, deity yoga is not prayer to an external deity; it is a direct practice of recognizing that your essential consciousness is not the limited individual "self" you believe you are, but is already Buddha-consciousness itself.

concepts.title: Deity Yoga: Imagining Yourself As Enlightened Being
concepts.excerpt: Normally in spirituality, you work on your defects. You identify your problems and try to fix them.

concepts.title: Embodying the Deity Before Invoking: Becoming the Frequency You're Calling
concepts.excerpt: When you invoke a deity in Tantra, you're not doing what most people think you're doing.

concepts.title: Ishta: The Chosen Ideal — Personal Deity, Unique Path
concepts.excerpt: Your ishta (also iṣṭa) is your chosen ideal — the particular form or name through which you relate to the divine.

concepts.title: Moon-Cycle Practice and Seasonal Sadhana: Aligning Practice With Natural Rhythms
concepts.excerpt: Most practitioners approach sadhana as if their consciousness should be constant—the same depth, the same capacity, the same accessibility every day regardless of external conditions.

concepts.title: Sadhana and the Constant Waning Moon — Temporal Consciousness in Kali Practice
concepts.excerpt: In Kali practice, the moon is not a metaphor for something else. The moon is time.

concepts.title: Tajaka System Architecture — Solar Return Apparatus
concepts.excerpt: A planet returns. Sun, having traversed 360°, comes back to the exact longitude he held at the moment of one's birth.

concepts.title: Muntha: Progressed Lagna in Tajaka
concepts.excerpt: Lagna in the natal chart stays fixed. The native is born with a specific lagna and that lagna defines structural references for life.

concepts.title: Harsha Bala, Pancha Vargeeya Bala, and Lord of the Year
concepts.excerpt: Tajaka annual analysis needs to know which planet matters most this year.

concepts.title: Sahams: The 36-Point Master Reference
concepts.excerpt: Every chart has twelve houses, nine planets, eight chara karakas. Most of the architecture comes pre-built.

concepts.title: Sixteen Tajaka Yogas
concepts.excerpt: Most natal-chart yogas read static planetary placements — Mars in the 10th, Jupiter in the 9th, the lord of one house in another.

concepts.title: Three Tajaka Annual Dasas: Patyayini, Mudda, Varsha Narayana
concepts.excerpt: Rao chapter 30 sets out three annual dashas: Patyayini (Tajaka-specific), Mudda (compressed Vimsottari), and Varsha Narayana (compressed Narayana).

concepts.title: Bādhaka — Eleven Forms of Misery and the Sign-Type Rule
concepts.excerpt: The 11th house in Vedic astrology gets popularly read as the "gains" house.

concepts.title: Deva Bādhaka — Nine-Graha Deity Mapping and Twelve-House Karma Table
concepts.excerpt: When the chart's Bādhaka-source is identified as Deva Bādhaka — the wrath of a deity — the chart names which deity through the Bādhakeśa's graha-quality and how the deity was wronged through the Bādhakeśa's house-position.

concepts.title: Sarpa Bādhaka — The Three Source-Types Read From Rāhu's Sign
concepts.excerpt: In Vedic cosmology, snakes (nāgas) are real beings who can curse and bless.

concepts.title: Preta Bādhaka — Unresolved Issues with the Recently Demised
concepts.excerpt: Preta = the recently demised, the wandering spirit not yet released. Preta Bādhaka is obstruction from unresolved-issues with someone who died.

concepts.title: Dṛṣṭi Bādhaka — Three Types Based on the Evil-Spirit's Desire
concepts.excerpt: The "evil eye" (dṛṣṭi) isn't a single mechanism. It splits into three distinct types based on what the looking-spirit wants from the native.

concepts.title: Abhicāra — Black Magic and the Mṛtyuñjaya Mantra as Praśna Mārga's Prime Remedy
concepts.excerpt: The eleventh and final form of misery in Harihara's Praśna Mārga is Abhicāra — active black magic or enemy action directed at the native.

concepts.title: Mother's Presence via 4L-from-Moon, Father's via 9L-from-Sun
concepts.excerpt: The mother's presence at the birth itself is guaranteed — without her body, the birth couldn't have happened.

concepts.title: Vāstu Faults — When You Buy Property at the Wrong Age
concepts.excerpt: You buy a house. Six months later you lose your job. Two years later you're still struggling.

concepts.title: Aparā Vidyā vs Parā Vidyā — The 3L, 12L, and Vidyā Architecture
concepts.excerpt: Vedic philosophy splits knowledge into two layers. Aparā Vidyā — "lower knowledge" — is what you need to navigate this world: language, math, social skills, profession, household management.

concepts.title: Bālāriṣṭa — Seven Tiers of Longevity, and the Sudarśana Cakra's Foundation
concepts.excerpt: Parāśara opens BPHS with a stark instruction. Before judging any chart, judge whether the native will survive infancy.

concepts.title: Maheśvara — The Śiva-Form That Detaches Soul From Mind
concepts.excerpt: Most chart-readers see the Maheśvara as a killer — a graha whose Daśā tends to bring death-or-major-transformation.

concepts.title: Kuṇḍalinī — 8th-House Raising Method and the Ketu Spontaneous-Awakening Trap
concepts.excerpt: Inside the body sit seven cakras, each a wheel of energy at a specific position along the spine and head.

concepts.title: Iṣṭa & Dharma Devata — 12th and 9th From Kārakāmsa
concepts.excerpt: Every chart has two appointed deities. One protects your journey through this life — your Dharma Devata, the protector of the path you came to walk.

concepts.title: Guru Devata — Bhrātṛkāraka in Navāmsa and the Eight Ātmaliṅga of Śiva
concepts.excerpt: Vedic philosophy teaches that the guru of the universe is Jupiter — and we approach Jupiter through worship of Sadāśiva.

concepts.title: Sūrya Doṣa — The Male-Heir Deficiency Pattern
concepts.excerpt: The Sun is the soul. The Sun is also the father-principle and the male-heir-principle.

concepts.title: Pitṛ Doṣa — Worshipping the Original-Progenitor Ṛṣi as Remedy
concepts.excerpt: The native's parents died early. The fortune-from-father lasted only briefly.

concepts.title: Śrāddha Doṣa — Saturn-Rāhu Conjunction Signals Unperformed Ancestral Rites
concepts.excerpt: In the chart of a Yugoslavian man born in 1969 — a mechanic whose mother died after he refused her care, who survived a fatal car accident, who endured a two-year criminal trial — Larsen reads a specific configuration: Saturn joined Rāhu in the 9th house = Śrāddha Doṣa.

concepts.title: Maraka, Rudra, Trishoola & Maheshvara Apparatus
concepts.excerpt: Four positions in a chart. Each named, each functional. The Maraka — the killer.

concepts.title: Three-Pairs and Eighth-Lord Longevity Methods
concepts.excerpt: How long will you live? Classical jyotish refuses to answer this question precisely — the texts repeatedly warn against telling natives their death-time — but it offers structural methods for estimating the range.

concepts.title: Niryaana Shoola Dasa & Shoola Dasa — Two Motions of Death
concepts.excerpt: Both dasas use Shoola — Shiva's trident — as the implement of death. Both predict the dasa-window in which the trident strikes.

concepts.title: Foss's Sanjay-Rath-Direct-Disciple Lineage Positioning
concepts.excerpt: In 2007, Andrew Foss walked into a small house a few miles north of the Konark Sun temple, on the Eastern coast of India.

concepts.title: The 108-Mantra-Per-Graha Remediation Apparatus
concepts.excerpt: Imagine a building with nine doors. Each door has 108 keys hanging beside it.

concepts.title: Foss's Four-Method Personal Mantra Selection System
concepts.excerpt: The 108-mantra-per-graha apparatus is the wall. Nine doors, 108 keys each, 972 mantras total.

concepts.title: Navagraha Stotra: The Hymn in Honour of the Planets
concepts.excerpt: Open any volume of Foss's Yoga of the Planets — Sūrya or Chandra or Budha or Śukra or Maṅgala or any of the four still to be ingested — and after the Dedication, the How-this-Book-Will-Help-You, the Find-Your-Personal-Mantras, the Journey, and the Notes-on-Pronunciation, you arrive at one short Sanskrit hymn:

concepts.title: Sūrya as Atman / Self / Soul-Grasper — The Foss 108-Mantra Layer
concepts.excerpt: Stand on a mountain in India before sunrise. The sky is still dark, but a thin greenish band appears at the horizon — not the Sun, but the charioteer of the Sun, Aruṇa, the dawn before the dawn.

concepts.title: Chandra as Mind / Mother / Soma-Nectar — The Foss 108-Mantra Layer
concepts.excerpt: If Sūrya is the dawn-Atman that precedes personal consciousness, Chandra is what does the personal consciousness — the mind, the heart, the feeling-body, the mother.

concepts.title: Budha (Mercury) as Intellect / Vishnu-Association / Trade-and-Medicine — The Foss 108-Mantra Layer
concepts.excerpt: Mercury's name in Sanskrit is Budha — the awakened one. Buddha (Gautama, the Sage of the Shakyas, born of royal lineage in Magadha) derives from the same root.

concepts.title: Śukra (Venus) as Essence / Shukra-Dhātu / Bhrigu-Lineage / Bhukti-Mukti — The Foss 108-Mantra Layer
concepts.excerpt: Whatever is the finest, most refined, or most precious of any animate or inanimate entity — that is Śukra.

concepts.title: Maṅgala (Mars) as Kuṇḍalinī Shakti / Skanda / Kshatriya-Protector — The Foss 108-Mantra Layer
concepts.excerpt: The first mantra of Mars opens like a riddle: om mahī-sutāya namaḥ — salutations to the son of the earth.

concepts.title: Guru as Bṛhaspati / Jupiter (Foss 108-Mantra Layer)
concepts.excerpt: Picture a swan offered a glass of milk and water mixed together. The story is that the swan drinks the milk and leaves the water — an impossible act, except as image.

concepts.title: Śani as Saturn / PashuPati: Karma-Discipline (Foss 108-Mantra Layer)
concepts.excerpt: Someone told Lord Shiva his Sade Sati was about to start — the seven-and-a-half years when Saturn passes over the twelfth, first, and second houses from the natal Moon.

concepts.title: Rāhu as North Node / Shadow (Foss 109-Mantra Layer)
concepts.excerpt: Across all nine volumes of Foss's Yoga of the Planets — 972 mantras for nine grahas — exactly one is a deliberate authorial exception.

concepts.title: Ketu as South Node / Mokṣa-Kāraka (Foss 108-Mantra Layer)
concepts.excerpt: The Brahma Sūtras — the great Vedantic text — end with a short aphorism that is repeated twice: anāvṛttih sabdādanāvṛttih sabdāt.

concepts.title: Three Mars Nakshatras Anchor the Vimshottari Sequence — Foss's Cross-Volume Discovery
concepts.excerpt: > SIGNAL page. — Foss explicitly reserves the full Vimshottari-derivation for the print edition of Yoga of the Planets.

concepts.title: The Bīja-Mantra Goddess-Power Sequence: Shrīṁ–Hrīṁ–Aiṁ–Aṁ (Sūrya 99-102)
concepts.excerpt: The 108 Sūrya mantras don't end with the 108th. They climax at the 99th-through-102nd — a four-mantra cluster that reveals what the entire 108 has been building toward.

concepts.title: Foss's Mantra-Primary Remedy Hierarchy vs. Other Vault Lineages
concepts.excerpt: The vault holds four practitioner-lineages on Vedic-astrology remediation: Kurczak/Fish (Kriya-Yoga + Viswa-Jyotirvid-Samgha), Pai (Frawley-Trivedi-Sutton-Rath cross-lineage), DiCara (Gauḍīya-Vaiṣṇava), and now Foss (Sanjay-Rath direct).

concepts.title: The 10 Vishnu Avatāras Graha-Assignment Scheme (Foss)
concepts.excerpt: A fish in the primordial ocean. Then a turtle (amphibian). Then a boar (mammal).

concepts.title: Rāhu-Ketu Axis as Inseparable Spinal Cosmology (Foss)
concepts.excerpt: A demon sneaks between the Sun and the Moon during the gods-and-demons churning of the ocean of consciousness.

concepts.title: Jupiter-Saturn Cosmic Clock: 54,000-Year Orbital Beat
concepts.excerpt: Foss buries one of the most specific cosmological-physical claims in the entire 9-volume corpus inside the Jupiter J4 Gochara commentary.

concepts.title: Foss Treats Sade Sati as Real Operational Period vs Kurczak/Fish Folk-Tradition Flag
concepts.excerpt: A practitioner walks into a Vedic-astrology consultation. The astrologer notes that Saturn is about to begin a 7.

concepts.title: Brāhmaṇa Not Caste but Knower of Brahman (Foss Philological Correction)
concepts.excerpt: Across the 9-volume Foss corpus, the same correction appears at multiple positions: "A Brāhmaṇa is not a member of a particular Hindu caste but one who has completely identified with the supreme wholeness."

concepts.title: Foss's Autobiographical Method as Witness: All Four Outer-Planet Volumes
concepts.excerpt: Foss discloses at Saturn S62: "Some pandits hold that Saturn is the greatest giver amongst the Grahas.

concepts.title: Foss's Interfaith Vedic-Bible Christianity Parallel Reading Method
concepts.excerpt: Across batch 2, Foss inserts five Bible citations at structurally specific positions: Sermon-on-the-Mount Luke 6:31 + Matthew 7:12 at Jupiter J73; Sodom-Gomorrah-Abraham-Lot at Rāhu R22; "Let he who has not sinned cast the first stone" (John 8:7) at Rāhu R47; Genesis-Eve-snake = Kundalini-Shakti at Rāhu R100; Bible-flood (Genesis 7) + James-Lovelock-Gaia at Ketu K81.

concepts.title: Foss's Ecology and Civilization Commentary as Ketu Ground
concepts.excerpt: Foss is at the Rishikesh Ashram.

concepts.title: Foss's Sanskrit-Etymology as Method
concepts.excerpt: Andrew Foss reads Sanskrit names the way a geologist reads sedimentary rock: every syllable is a compressed layer of meaning, and if you separate the syllables you find a fossil-record of the cosmology the name belongs to.

concepts.title: Foss's Modern-Physics ↔ Vedic-Cosmology Parallels Methodology
concepts.excerpt: Andrew Foss has a PhD in Computing Science from the University of Alberta and is an Oxford University Physics graduate with publications in Nature and other leading scientific journals.

concepts.title: Foss's Mantra Acoustic-Phonological Theory: Sounds-as-Vibrational-Form-of-States
concepts.excerpt: Most contemplative traditions that use chant or sustained-recitation make a soft claim: repeating words with attention is good for concentration and helpful for the practitioner's state.

concepts.title: Foss's Sacred Geography of Jyotish — The Konark-Kollur-Varanasi Pilgrimage Architecture
concepts.excerpt: Open any Foss volume and the "Journey" section is reproduced verbatim.

concepts.title: Foss's Caveat-and-Safety Architecture for Mantra Practice
concepts.excerpt: A 972-mantra apparatus that activates the vibrational form of specific consciousness-states is not a toy.

concepts.title: Foss's Correspondence-Table System: Color / Metal / Gem / Body / Direction / Flower / Animal per Graha
concepts.excerpt: The 972-mantra apparatus operates with a dense network of per-graha correspondences: gold for Sun, silver for Moon, copper for Mars; ruby for Sun, pearl for Moon, coral for Mars; jasmine for Moon and Venus, red roses for Mars, Chāmpeya (Rose-apple) for Mercury; lion-vāhana for Mercury and Venus, ram for Mars, deer for Moon; North-facing Mercury, East-facing Sun, South-facing Yama.

concepts.title: Foss as First English-Language Commentator on the 108-Mantra-Per-Graha System
concepts.excerpt: Andrew Foss documents in the "Sources and Acknowledgements" section of every Yoga of the Planets volume: "While these lists are well known to traditional astrologers in India, I only found two places where they had been printed."

concepts.title: Foss's Reincarnation-and-Longevity Operational Framework
concepts.excerpt: Vedic-astrology traditions handle death-and-rebirth as part of standard chart-reading, not as separate spiritual-discipline.

concepts.title: Foss's Stephen Hawking Black-Hole Vedic-Cosmology Integration
concepts.excerpt: Foss opens the Jupiter volume at J1 with the Eddington-Einstein 1919 eclipse-verification anecdote: a young physicist sailing to Principe island off West Africa, photographing stars during a total eclipse to verify Einstein's prediction that light bends around the Sun.

concepts.title: Foss's Yoga Vasiṣṭha as Vedic-Physics Precision-Language Quotes
concepts.excerpt: Foss places the Yoga Vasiṣṭha Queen-Līlā cosmic-tour passages at K105 — mantra position 105 of 108 — near-finale of the Ketu volume.

concepts.title: Lineage as Operational Necessity for Sūtra Interpretation (Foss)
concepts.excerpt: Foss states it directly at Ketu K39, in the Jaimini-Gotraja commentary on the Jaimini Upadesha Sūtras: "Some people think that by reading the Sūtras and their translations, they can understand their import.

concepts.title: Foss's Mundane-and-Collective-Event Astrological-Correlate Methodology
concepts.excerpt: Foss inserts brief mundane-event-correlate references across batch 2: the Middle-East-turmoil starting when Rāhu entered Gemini on the last day of July 2000 ("Second Intifada" started September 2000); North-East-USA-London-Italy blackouts after Rāhu entered Krittikā in February 2003; Hurricane Katrina year 2005 after Rāhu entered watery Pisces in April 2005.

concepts.title: Abhijit: The Intercalary Nakshatra
concepts.excerpt: In the Bhagavad Gita, Lord Krishna runs through a long catalogue of what he is among various things in the universe.

concepts.title: Ancient Equinoxes: Shatabhishaj-Krittika-Anuradha 5000-BCE Archaeoastronomy
concepts.excerpt: Modern astronomy can back-calculate the positions of stars at any historical-moment using the precession-of-the-equinoxes (a slow 26,000-year cycle in which the Earth's axial-tilt traces a circle through the stars).

concepts.title: Nakshatra Orientation: Adho / Urdhwa / Tiryanga Mukha
concepts.excerpt: Every nakshatra "faces" one of three directions: downward (Adho Mukha), upward (Urdhwa Mukha), or straight forward / level (Tiryanga Mukha).

concepts.title: Nakshatra Pada to Navamsha: The 108 Sub-Divisions
concepts.excerpt: The 27 nakshatras each have 4 padas (quarters / sub-divisions).

concepts.title: Nakshatra Purusha: The Body of Vishnu Mapped to the 27 Lunar Mansions
concepts.excerpt: In the Vishnu Purana, Sage Pulastya tells Narada: "All the constellations dwell in different parts of Lord Vishnu's body."

concepts.title: Nakshatra Remediation Methodology: The Meta-Protocol
concepts.excerpt: Most Jyotish-remedies are presented as isolated prescriptions — chant this mantra, wear this gemstone, fast on this day.

concepts.title: Shakti / Basis Above / Basis Below: Pai's Operational Framework
concepts.excerpt: If the 27 nakshatras are 27 different operational mechanisms in the cosmos, Pai's lineage provides a single diagnostic schema that decodes every one of them in the same way.

concepts.title: Sapta Shalaka Chakra: The Nakshatra Vedha (Affliction) System
concepts.excerpt: > Nakshatra opposite to each other causes Nakshatra Vedha. For example, Bharani causes Vedha to Magha and vice versa.

concepts.title: 32 Forms of Ganesha → Nakshatra Mapping
concepts.excerpt: There are 32 traditional iconographic forms of Lord Ganesha. There are 27 nakshatras (plus Abhijit, sometimes counted as the 28th).

concepts.title: Tri-Murti Nakshatra Assignment: Brahma / Vishnu / Shiva
concepts.excerpt: Every operation in the cosmos belongs to one of three functions. Something gets created (the Brahma function).

concepts.title: Gana: Deva / Manushya / Rakshasa Temperament Classification
concepts.excerpt: Every person you meet falls into one of three camps without quite trying.

concepts.title: Yoni: The 14-Animal Totem Compatibility System
concepts.excerpt: Two people meet, fall in love, talk about marriage. The astrologer pulls out their charts and looks first at the Yoni — the animal-totem of each natal nakshatra.

concepts.title: DiCara's Recursive Deselfing Authorship
concepts.excerpt: You read 2,900 lines of DiCara's book and the author has been steadily present the whole way through — his voice, his arguments, his Gauḍīya lineage commitments, his choices about what to highlight.

concepts.title: DiCara's Structural Cross-Star Indexing: The 27 Nakshatras as a System, Not a List
concepts.excerpt: Pai treats each nakshatra as a closed mythological territory — Bharani has Yama, Krittika has Agni, Rohini has Brahma, and inside each chapter the deity is the main character with supporting cast.

concepts.title: DiCara's Three Misconceptions: Stars Are Not Signs, Stars Have No Planetary Lords, Deities Empower Nakshatras
concepts.excerpt: Open a popular Vedic astrology book.
